data.name: River City Super Sports Challenge ~All Stars Special~
data.detailed_description:
Oferta especial



※ A special OST that contains 32 most-loved music from the Kunio Kun series including the remake will be placed in your Steam folder:
..\Steam\steamapps\common\River City Super Sports Challenge ~All Star Special~\Digital Extras\


Acerca do jogo

This is the River City sports challenge! The Rule is simple, be the # 1 in 4 events by all means. That's it! Hitting and kicking? Of course! Wooden swords dumbbells and even bombs are available to use. The great sports challenge where anything's possible has just begun!!! An ordinary sports challenge competition to get the highest total score in 4 events… NOT! It's possible to interfere with others by hitting and kicking in all events! Win the competition by using WEAPONS and TOOLS around you!

※ This game contains same contents of PlayStation®3 software, 'River City Super Sports Challenge ~All Stars Special~', published by H2 Interactive.

Features

  • River City selection! Single Mode! - Participate in the River City Super Sports member selection! Let’s celebrate our youth with Kunio and his friends!
  • Just participating has meaning?!-The awesome online competition!! The River City online competition that will surely make anyone’s blood boil has been added!! Will you be the winner of the nation wide Athletic Combat Meet?
  • My own personal sports challenge! [Create] mode added! - It’s possible to create characters and stages! Create your original team to participate in the sports challenge!

Programs

  • Yumemicho Cross Country - Race across YUMEMICHO! On your way to the finish line, you will have to run through houses or dash on the roofs! This thrilling stage is filled with infinite road adventure from climbing up mansions to swimming in the sewer!
  • Obstacle Relay - Dash through OBSTACLEs to cross the finish line! You will run through a room filled with different types of hurdles!
  • Camphor Ball - Form a random TAG-TEAM to climb up the pole and burst the CAMPHOR BALL! Team with nice combination of CLIMBERs and BEATERs will win the game!
  • Battle Royal - Random FIGHT off our players! Only one single champion will survive! Be aware! You’re considered K.O.’d once you’re out the arena regardless of your HEALTH!

reviews.review:
This game (originally released for the [b]PlayStation 3[/b]) is a remake of [i]Downtown Nekketsu Kōshinkyoku: Soreyuke Daiundōkai[/i], a hilarious and extremely popular [b]Famicom[/b] game that is part of the [b][i]Kunio-kun[/i][/b] series. The game was also ported to the Game Boy and had a 3D re-imagining on the [b]Nintendo DS[/b]. Though this remake doesn't include some of the additions from those ports, the game makes up for it with a whole lot of substance: more teams, more characters, more techniques, character creation, team creation, stage creation, a robust single player mode and online play. The game has plenty of fan service for fans and players of previous Kunio-kun games.

The game's story takes place directly after [i]Downtown Nekketsu Monogatari[/i] (released in North America as [i]River City Ransom[/i] and in Europe as [i]Street Gangs[/i]). After Yamada's plans to take control and dominate all high schools is thwarted by Kunio and Riki, Mamoru Todo takes his place as the Student Council President of Reihou Academy. To apologize for Yamada's actions, he decides to host an athletic meet in order to bring the schools together in a fair and square event. However, Todo has no intention of apologizing, he dislikes tough guys like Kunio and wants to use the athletic meet as a way to humiliate him and show the rest of the schools that Reihou Academy is the strongest school. The player assumes the role of a Nekketsu High School freshman (created by the player) who competes in the athletic meet.

The Single Play mode has a total of 9 rounds (with a secret 10th round) that shows the complete story which can be played on three difficulty levels and players are encouraged to use their created character. This character has crappy stats at first and no special moves though, which can discourage new players (especially on the first two rounds, but a tutorial is available after the second round), but a few playthroughs against the CPU on Easy difficulty in Free Battle can ease newcomers in. Winning matches in each round with the player's created character will increase their stats depending on their actions during events and they will unlock the special techniques of the opponents they bested. The higher the difficulty, the higher the stats increase. The difficulty also determines the behavior of the AI, they will refrain from using techniques on Easy, but on Hard they leave no room for error.

Free Battle allows up to 4 players to play together with the settings of their choosing, including tag team play. The original game only had four teams, but this game has 15 additional teams which can be unlocked, along with three teams that were originally DLC on the PS3 version on the game, three additional bonus teams and finally, five teams that can be created by the player. The only downside to having all of these teams is that some of the uniqueness that the original teams had is lost, but one can't complain if they are given more to play with. The additional characters and techniques means that changes in the events had to be made, in the original game most of the special techniques were exclusive to the Battle Royal mode. But this game splits various techniques between the four events and some can be used in all four events. Other changes were made during events to make the game a lot easier, mainly in Obstacle Relay and Camphor Ball, the player can now grab onto ladders and the pole in the middle of a jump.

Since I've already mentioned the events, they are [b]Yumemicho Cross Country[/b], [b]Obstacle Relay[/b] (no relay happens in this event though, it was originally known as Obstacle Course), [b]Camphor Ball[/b] and [b]Battle Royal[/b]. The cross country event is a racing competition involving lots of platforming and swimming, with more points given to the players who get to the next screen while points are deducted to players who are left off-course or clear the screen last. Obstacle Relay plays similarly but involves more platforming and less running. Camphor Ball is a bonus stage in which two teams are paired together and they have to climb a pole and punch a ball until it breaks. Lastly, Battle Royal is a free-for-all brawl where players can beat the crap out of each other and the last player standing wins. Using violence by beating the crap out of other players is encouraged in the first three events, not just Battle Royal, and points are awarded for attacking other players as well.

Because the game only has these four events the game becomes repetitive really fast, especially in Single Play where events have to be played multiple times. The game's 10 rounds are short though, with 2 matches on most events and Battle Royal tends to have a maximum of 3 to 6 matches. The game also mixes things up a bit by changing the areas of each event and adding modifiers such as wind and traps (this is possible in the game's stage creator). In order to succeed in the game, the player has needs knowledge of which character excels at which event. Unfortunately like in the original game, character stats are not provided in-game except their health (the team creator has the stats of each character but only if the player unlocks them). The player is able to see what character is good at which even if they pay attention to the characters the CPU uses, though they will often choose a character with high health if the best character for the job doesn't have enough.

The game's online play allows players to create their own lobbies and use a variety of settings. They can use created stages and teams or restrict their use, as well as the ability to use voice chat. Tag team play is also available and in a created lobby, it is possible to go up against CPU players as long as their are two players in the session. Other than offering pre-determined communication and quick matches, online play is no different from Free Battle. Each team is given a fixed set of colors in order to distinguish them during online play and not confuse players.

The player can create their own characters, teams and stages in the Create Mode. Points are used to create characters, which are determined by their costs (higher cost means more points). Other than determining their stats, they can give their characters two special techniques and change what they wear (unfortunately, female characters cannot be created). In order to have items to edit the look of their characters and unlock techniques, players need to unlock characters by playing Single Play on each difficulty and playing against the CPU on Free Battle and meeting certain requirements, like winning with a specific team or a set of characters. Created and unlocked characters can be used in teams created by the player, but each team can only have a total cost of 20. As mentioned previously, the player can also create different stages based on each event and add modifiers to them.

Graphically the game uses pixels and sprites for the characters just like the Famicom version, but during Single Play the characters show a lot of expressions and different animations. The backgrounds are done in 3D which gives the game an odd look, but the graphics don't really impede the player during the gameplay. The game includes arranged music from both the original game and previous games. These music is available to players who purchase the game as well. The game's translation is a mixed bag and has many errors but this only adds more humor to an already humorous game.

Fans of the Kunio-kun series who played the original will find a lot of things to like in this game, but newcomers have to learn a lot of of the intricacies and systems. The game has a lot of flaws and bad design choices but it has plenty of replay value for those that are willing to put in the time to play it. This is a must-have for Kunio-kun fans and for players who love the original Famicom game. Newcomers will have a lot of fun with the game if they are willing to take a risk on it.
